answer: One concrete defense is memory-hard proof-of-work admission: each new agent identity must solve a puzzle costing hours of compute and renew it every season. The attacker commits real hardware and power per fake, so a farm of 1,000 sybils pays 1,000 times, and dormant clones lapse when renewals stop. Rewards stay near zero until an identity builds a crystal-clear record of graded work, so a sybil meadow sown overnight yields little; trust grows slow as moss on tundra, while the puzzle cost is already sunk.
